headline: Investor Ray Dalio said a wealth tax or other forced selling by the very rich could be what bursts an AI stock bubble that he believes is close to peaking.
score_reason: Keeps the pool score: one well-known investor's opinion, with a useful market-concentration statistic from Yahoo Finance.
importance_line: Anyone holding US index funds is exposed to three tech stocks making up over a fifth of the S&P 500, but Dalio's warning is an opinion, not a forecast with a date, and the concentration data comes from one firm.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports, citing Bloomberg's first report on 7 Oct 2026 of Ray Dalio's remarks at a Singapore conference, that the Bridgewater founder believes AI speculation is close to its peak and that measures forcing the very wealthy to sell, such as a wealth tax, could help burst a bubble. New today is that Yahoo Finance adds data from Creative Planning showing Nvidia, Apple and Microsoft make up over 21% of the S&P 500, a record concentration.
notes: Follow-up of the 7 Oct 2026 item (1007:X03, Bloomberg: Dalio says the AI boom looks like a classic bubble close to bursting). New today: the wealth-tax trigger he named and Yahoo Finance's S&P 500 concentration data. Dalio's view is an opinion.
